title: LUMC CodeMeta profile
description: A profile of CodeMeta 3.1. Generated from profile/lumc-codemeta.yaml by scripts/build_schema.py; edit that file, not this one.

@context.title: JSON-LD context
@context.description: Must reference a CodeMeta 3.x context. The context is what gives the property names in this file a defined meaning.

@type.title: Node type
@type.description: SoftwareSourceCode for software distributed as source, SoftwareApplication for software distributed only as an executable or a service.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the item (software, Organization)
name.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: Text.

description.title: Description
description.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: Text.

version.title: Version
version.description: A semantic version is preferred. For software with no releases, a full Git commit hash identifies the state exactly.
version.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: Number or Text.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: A persistent identifier for this release. A DOI is preferred; mint one by publishing a release with the Zenodo-GitHub integration enabled. A Git tag URL is accepted for software that will never be formally published.
identifier.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: PropertyValue or URL.

author.title: Author
author.description: Everyone who should be credited, in citation order. Give each person an ORCID in `@id`, and each affiliation a ROR in its own `@id`.
author.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: Organization or Person.

license.title: License
license.description: An SPDX identifier URL, for example https://spdx.org/licenses/Apache-2.0. For a license with no SPDX identifier, use a CreativeWork node carrying its name and URL.
license.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: CreativeWork or URL.

codeRepository.title: Code repository
codeRepository.description: A link to the repository where the un-compiled, human readable code and related code is located (SVN, GitHub, CodePlex, institutional GitLab instance, etc.).
codeRepository.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: URL.

programmingLanguage.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the codemeta vocabulary: ComputerLanguage or Text.

applicationCategory.description: The kind of software. A term from the bio.tools tool-type vocabulary makes the record discoverable in that registry.

schema:featureList.title: Feature list
schema:featureList.description: What the software does. EDAM operation URLs drive semantic search in bio.tools and ELIXIR infrastructure; free text is accepted when no term fits. Keep the `schema:` prefix.
schema:featureList.$comment: Generated by scripts/build_schema.py. Type from the schema.org vocabulary: Text or URL.

author.description: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.

dateCreated.description: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.

dateModified.title: Date modified

editor.title: Editor
editor.description: Specifies the Person who edited the CreativeWork.

encoding.title: Encoding
encoding.description: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork. This property is a synonym for associatedMedia. Supersedes encodings.

fileFormat.title: File format
fileFormat.description: Media type, typically MIME format (see IANA site) of the content e.g. application/zip of a SoftwareApplication binary. In cases where a CreativeWork has several media type representations, 'encoding' can be used to indicate each MediaObject alongside particular fileFormat information. Unregistered or niche file formats can be indicated instead via the most appropriate URL, e.g. defining Web page or a Wikipedia entry.

propertyID.title: Property i d
propertyID.description: A commonly used identifier for the characteristic represented by the property, e.g. a manufacturer or a standard code for a property. propertyID can be (1) a prefixed string, mainly meant to be used with standards for product properties; (2) a site-specific, non-prefixed string (e.g. the primary key of the property or the vendor-specific ID of the property), or (3) a URL indicating the type of the property, either pointing to an external vocabulary, or a Web resource that describes the property (e.g. a glossary entry). Standards bodies should promote a standard prefix for the identifiers of properties from their standards.

value.title: Value
value.description:
The value of a [[QuantitativeValue]] (including [[Observation]]) or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
